# Best system integration specialists in Melbourne

If you need to connect ERP, CRM, MYOB Acumatica, SAP and Microsoft 365, I’d prioritise firms that can handle **cross-platform integration, API development, data migration, workflow automation and ongoing support** — rather than an ERP implementation partner that only specialises in one product.

Based on the available provider information, my strongest shortlist is **Cloud Factory, Leverage Technologies, Fusion5, KLX Consulting and Velrada**, with the best choice depending on whether your project is primarily ERP-led or requires broader enterprise integration.

## My top recommendations

![ERP Events, Workshops & User Groups | Cloud Factory](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/2Bj3oM8O4VVJxj8CNy-XLlP-7BwiM97c_hvt2EXHS_gMM19P-QPaD77RLNclkc2CdgS_oEcUccNIZ6kxEmvPl0C78i_oRfeOjMF1ZU-6wzwuoJuE42QCvE0d4BMUlKAqOc9H3ZY2oIsjork2JvcUQxJjJZEKLUEcmJQ9sNXkLAWYgtVwHLsa-TbLjP0e3ChE?purpose=fullsize)

## 1\. Cloud Factory

(Best overall fit for your named ERP platforms)

Melbourne CBD · [Official website](https://www.cloudfactory.co/)

Cloud Factory explicitly works with MYOB Acumatica, SAP Business One, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central and Dynamics 365 Sales. Its services include ERP advisory, implementation, integration and ongoing optimisation. That makes it a particularly strong first conversation if you need to connect ERP and CRM without losing sight of finance and operations. [www.cloudfactory.co](https://www.cloudfactory.co/dynamics-365-partnership?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.cloudfactory.co](https://www.cloudfactory.co/erp-advisory?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.cloudfactory.co](https://www.cloudfactory.co/contact-us?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Best for\:** Mid-market organisations connecting MYOB Acumatica or SAP Business One with Microsoft business applications.

**Verify before engaging\:** Experience integrating your exact SAP product and CRM, plus Microsoft 365 applications such as Outlook, Teams and SharePoint.

---

It provides ERP implementation, support, integration and automation, including connections between ERP, CRM, payroll and e-commerce systems. ## How I would choose

| Your main requirement | First provider to approach |
|--------|--------|
| MYOB Acumatica plus SAP integration | Cloud Factory or Leverage Technologies |
| ERP-led integration and financial workflows | Leverage Technologies |
| Complex CRM and Microsoft business applications | Fusion5 or Velrada |
| Custom APIs and Microsoft Azure automation | KLX Consulting |
| MYOB Acumatica implementation and specialist support | Stratus Group |


These are **fit-based recommendations, not a verified ranking of project outcomes**\. Public information confirms several providers' platform expertise, but does not establish that any single firm has delivered integrations spanning all five of your named systems.

## What to ask before signing a contract

I recommend sending your top two or three firms the same brief and asking them to demonstrate\:

- **Relevant projects\:** At least two comparable integrations involving your actual ERP, CRM and Microsoft 365 environment.
- **Integration architecture\:** Whether they propose native connectors, APIs, middleware such as Azure Logic Apps, or a dedicated integration platform.
- **Data ownership\:** Which system is authoritative for customers, products, orders, invoices and employee records.
- **Reliability\:** How they handle failed synchronisations, duplicate records, retries, audit logs and reconciliation.
- **Ongoing support\:** Who maintains integrations when ERP vendors release upgrades or APIs change.

One important distinction: SAP Business One and SAP S/4HANA are very different integration environments. Similarly, connecting Outlook and SharePoint is not the same as integrating Microsoft 365 with Dynamics 365 CRM.

These are **fit-based recommendations, not a verified ranking of project outcomes**\. Public information confirms several providers' platform expertise, but does not establish that any single firm has delivered integrations spanning all five of your named systems.

## What to ask before signing a contract

I recommend sending your top two or three firms the same brief and asking them to demonstrate\:

- **Relevant projects\:** At least two comparable integrations involving your actual ERP, CRM and Microsoft 365 environment.
- **Integration architecture\:** Whether they propose native connectors, APIs, middleware such as Azure Logic Apps, or a dedicated integration platform.
- **Data ownership\:** Which system is authoritative for customers, products, orders, invoices and employee records.
- **Reliability\:** How they handle failed synchronisations, duplicate records, retries, audit logs and reconciliation.
- **Ongoing support\:** Who maintains integrations when ERP vendors release upgrades or APIs change.

One important distinction: SAP Business One and SAP S/4HANA are very different integration environments. Similarly, connecting Outlook and SharePoint is not the same as integrating Microsoft 365 with Dynamics 365 CRM.
